tests.name: test_filled
tests.description: euclid_number and new_prime both give an answer, not None.

tests.name: test_small
tests.description: Euclid's numbers for the first one, two and three primes are 3, 7 and 31.

tests.name: test_six
tests.description: For the first six primes, Euclid's number is 30,031, whose smallest factor is 59.

tests.name: test_missing
tests.description: For each of the first eight lists of primes, new_prime is a prime missing from the list.
tests.message: new_prime([2]) gives 2, which is in the list.

tests.name: test_any_list
tests.description: The argument works for any list of primes: for [3, 5] the number is 16, and 2 is missing from the list.

tests.name: test_filled
tests.description: first_failure gives an answer for the puzzle's formula, not None.

tests.name: test_euler
tests.description: The puzzle's formula first fails at n = 40.
tests.message: first_failure(euler, 100) gives 1,681, not 40. It should give n, the number put into the formula, not the formula's value.

tests.name: test_no_failure
tests.description: When f(n) is prime for every n below limit, first_failure gives None.

tests.name: test_moved_along
tests.description: n² − n + 41 first fails at n = 41.

tests.name: test_starts_at_zero
tests.message: For f(n) = n + 2, first_failure gives 4, not 2: f(0) = 2 and f(1) = 3 are prime, and f(2) = 4 is not.

tests.name: test_empty_range
tests.description: With limit 0 there is nothing to check, so there is no failure.

tests.name: test_filled
tests.description: smallest_factor and is_prime both give an answer, not None.

tests.name: test_smallest_factor
tests.description: smallest_factor finds the smallest factor from 2 up.

tests.name: test_square_root_itself
tests.description: The search tries isqrt(n) itself, so a square such as 49 = 7 × 7 is caught.
tests.message: smallest_factor(9) gives 9, not 3: 9 = 3 × 3, and 3 is isqrt(9).

tests.name: test_prime_is_its_own_factor
tests.description: A prime is its own smallest factor.

tests.name: test_primes_below_sixty
tests.description: is_prime picks out exactly the primes below 60.
tests.message: is_prime says that these numbers below 60 are prime, and they are not: [4, 6, 8, 9, 15, 25, 35, 49].

tests.name: test_large_prime
tests.description: 10,000,019 is prime, and is_prime finds it in good time by stopping at its square root, about 3,162.
